name: Cardone
classification_notes: Contemporary interpretation of early Scottish modern (Scotch Roman) faces. High-contrast, vertical-stress design with ball terminals, bracketed serifs and long tapered stems. Five weights drawn independently rather than interpolated. The Micro subfamily strips back detail for sub-8pt text, giving it a more mechanical, regularised character. Rich OpenType feature set including oldstyle figures, contextual alternates, fractions, stylistic sets for arrows, ampersand, numero and alternate J and Q forms.
summary: A Scotch Roman revival without the reverence: five independently drawn weights and a dedicated Micro cut, built for demanding editorial work.
description: Cardone takes the vertical stress, high contrast and ball terminals of early Scottish modern typefaces as its starting point, then departs from strict revival with bracketed serifs and softer transitions that hold up in continuous text. Fátima Lázaro spent five years developing the family at EsadType in Amiens, drawing each weight from scratch so that every style has its own distinct character rather than feeling mechanically interpolated. A Micro variant – leaner and more mechanical – handles text below eight points while remaining legible at display sizes.
foundry_blurb: 205TF describes Cardone as a singular interpretation of early Scotch Roman faces, where ample curves play against the brutality of the lines and the verticality of the axis. Each style is pushed toward extreme simplicity and efficiency, both in structure and in every formal detail.

name: Henry
classification_notes: Historical revival based on Henri Parmentier's 1914–1926 Deberny & Peignot Garamond engravings, calibrated for medium text sizes (9–14pt). Proportions are lean and slightly narrow with subtle Art Nouveau inflections in the z, a, J and Q. Roman and Italic only.
summary: A lean Garalde revival drawn from Henri Parmentier's 1914–1926 Deberny & Peignot Garamond engravings, with a slim precision and subtle Art Nouveau eccentricities that set it apart from conventional Garamond revivals.
description: Henry is Matthieu Cortat's revival of a specific and under-referenced source: Parmentier's early 20th-century Garamond engravings for Deberny & Peignot, calibrated for medium text sizes rather than the cloth-paper conditions of the 16th century. The result is a narrow, elegant Garalde with Art Nouveau inflections – an angled z, winding a and J, a looped Q, and an italic with changing rhythm and playful ligatures – that distinguish it from more conventional Garamond interpretations. Two styles with an extensive OpenType feature set make it well-suited to careful book and editorial setting.
foundry_blurb: 205TF describes Henry as a personal reinterpretation of the Garamond engraved for Deberny & Peignot by Henri Parmentier between 1914 and 1926 under Georges Peignot, based on medium text sizes of 9 to 14pt. The original project sought to recover the grace of Claude Garamont's letterforms while accounting for modern wood-pulp paper rather than the cloth-based papers of the 16th century.

name: Maax Micro
classification_notes: Optical size variant of Maax, a neo-grotesque with four stylistic alternate sets spanning standard all-purpose, geometric, modern and grotesk styles. Inktraps engineered to keep counterforms open below 8pt become visible angular features at display sizes. Three weights with matching italics; variable font versions added in 2026.
summary: An optical size cut of Maax that uses inktraps to keep counterforms open below 8pt, those same traps reading as angular architectural detail when the type is enlarged.
description: Maax Micro is a precision optical size variant of Damien Gautier's Maax, built for small and very small settings. Inktraps – invisible below 8pt – prevent ink spread from closing letterform counterforms, while revealing a sharp, almost extravagant character at display sizes. Three weights with matching italics carry the full OpenType feature set of the parent family, including four stylistic sets covering standard, geometric, modern and grotesque alternates.
foundry_blurb: Maax is a sans-serif whose design deliberately avoids optical corrections, lending it a directness that can suffer at small sizes when counterforms clog. Maax Micro addresses this with inktraps that activate below 8pt, absorbing excess ink and keeping the forms open while remaining invisible at that scale. The same traps that preserve legibility at micro sizes reveal surprising geometric forms when set large.

name: Immortel
classification_notes: A four-variant text family organised around the Hippocratic theory of humours rather than conventional weight gradations: Infra (phlegmatic, after Granjon's 16th-century Gros Cicéro), Colera (choleric, after Jannon and Ganeau's Vendôme), Vena (sanguine, after Rosart's 18th-century work), and Acedia (melancholic, synthesising Dürer's Melencolia I). All four variants share identical set widths, x-heights, ascenders and descenders, enabling direct substitution without layout disruption. Infra and Vena each offer two grades — G1 and G2 — providing tonal variation for different papers and printing conditions while preserving line length. A dual italic system appears in Infra and Vena: Median (slightly inclined, for extended reading) and Italic (sharper angle with ornate details). Available as 16 static styles and six variable fonts.
summary: A four-variant text serif structured around the Hippocratic humours, each subfamily drawing from a different century of French type history while sharing identical metrics for seamless editorial interchange.
description: Developed at ANRT Nancy from 2016 and released by 205TF in 2021, Immortel organises its four subfamilies — Infra, Colera, Vena, Acedia — around the bodily humours rather than conventional weight gradations, each referencing a distinct historical engraver: Granjon, Jannon, Rosart and Dürer. Consistent set widths across all variants allow one to stand in for another without disrupting layout, while Infra and Vena offer two grades and a Median italic alongside a full cursive for fine editorial control. The family spans 16 static styles and six variable fonts with support for over 200 languages.
foundry_blurb: 205TF present Immortel as a rethinking of type family architecture: rather than weight gradations, four temperamentally distinct variants each embody one of the Hippocratic humours and reference a different historical period of type engraving, bound by shared metrics that make them interchangeable within a single composed page.

name: Milling
classification_notes: Single-line typeface engineered from CNC tool-path logic. Three construction modes – Simplex, Duplex, Triplex – build letterform weight by adding machining passes rather than varying stroke contrast in the conventional sense. Monolinear at its core; Triplex introduces contrast through layered passes. Geometric in structure throughout.
summary: Milling translates CNC tool-path logic into typography, building letterform weight through repeated machining passes rather than conventional stroke contrast, and shipping in four formats for use across engraving, cutting and print alike.
description: Born from Tanguy Vanlaeys's seven-year research at ANRT Nancy, Milling treats each letter as a sequence of tool paths rather than an outlined shape – Simplex, Duplex and Triplex variants add passes to build weight and contrast. It ships in single-line, CAD, OpenType and toolpath-contour formats, making it usable for laser cutting and CNC engraving as well as conventional typesetting. Variable fonts for Simplex and Triplex give continuous control over stroke width, with 14 stylistic sets for alternate letter and punctuation forms.
foundry_blurb: 205TF frames Milling as a typeface adapted to numerical machining but not confined by it – Vanlaeys planned tool movements rather than sculpted letterforms, and the result meets the requirements of CNC engraving while leaving graphic designers free to experiment across print, screen and physical media.

name: Exposure
classification_notes: A variable typeface whose single custom axis simulates photographic exposure rather than conventional weight, width or slant. At zero the letterforms are clean and legible; at negative values counterforms fill and blacken; at positive values strokes dissolve into stencil-like outlines. Structurally the base design reads as a humanist display face with a generous x-height, developed for headline use across its full axis range. Tagged as stencil/serif by independent catalogues, reflecting the overexposed end of the axis rather than the neutral base.
summary: A variable display face by Federico Parra Barrios whose single axis shifts letterforms across a photographic exposure spectrum – from ink-flooded black at -100 to dissolved, stencil-like outlines at +100.
description: Developed over 2.5 years at the Atelier national de recherche typographique in Nancy, Exposure replaces the conventional weight-width-slant model with a single light intensity axis spanning -100 to +100. At zero the face reads cleanly for headlines; push toward either pole and the letterforms either fill with darkness until counterforms vanish, or bleach into near-ghostly outlines. Each of the 1,380 glyphs was drawn individually to handle the transformation – the typeface took first prize at the CDA54 type design awards in 2023.
foundry_blurb: 205TF describes Exposure as a reimagining of the variable axis itself: rather than adjusting weight, width or optical size, the exposure index controls the intensity of light falling on sculptural three-dimensional letters. Underexpose and the counterforms fill almost to illegibility; overexpose and parts of the letterform disappear as if burned by the light.

name: Muoto
classification_notes: Geometric sans with deliberate humanist warmth – full curves and considered proportions distinguish it from cold neutralists like Helvetica or Univers. The Alvar Aalto design philosophy and collaborative commission by Base Design give it a hybrid humanist-geometric character that sits closer to Graphik than to Futura.
summary: A warmly modernist geometric sans from Matthieu Cortat, spanning six weights, four widths and a monospaced companion, with its design grounded in Alvar Aalto's principle of functional warmth.
description: Commissioned by Base Design to succeed their Basetica, Muoto pairs full curves with solid stems to produce a sans that reads as functional without feeling cold. The family covers four widths – Ultra Condensed, Condensed, Regular and Extended – across six weights and matching italics in both static and variable formats, the latter expanded in 2022. A monospaced sibling, Muoto Mono, extends the system into tabular and coding contexts.
foundry_blurb: 205TF describe Muoto as the synthesis of a sensitive, human approach to modernist design, combining full curves and solid stems to show that functionalism can be warm and effective. The typeface draws on Alvar Aalto's belief in creating simple, undecorated things that remain in harmony with the human being.

name: Alcalá Xtra
classification_notes: Renaissance-rooted text serif drawing on type from the Complutensian Polyglot Bible (1520). Alcalá Xtra is the small-size-optimised edition of Gautier's parent Alcalá family, distinguished by a more generous x-height that makes it read visually larger than its nominal point size. Five focused styles – Roman, Italic, Bold, Mono and Stencil – each address a distinct function: the Mono introduces fixed-width rhythm for editorial layouts; the Stencil extends the design to identity and signage at varied scales. No intermediate weights; the family is deliberately lean.
summary: Damien Gautier's 31-year text serif project, rooted in the Complutensian Polyglot Bible, reissued in 2026 with a taller x-height and Mono and Stencil companions designed for press and editorial work at small sizes.
description: Alcalá Xtra is the small-text edition of Gautier's historical family, first sketched in 1995 from type in the Complutensian Polyglot Bible and now in its fourth iteration. The enhanced x-height makes it appear visually larger than its point size, a genuine advantage at the sizes typical in newspaper and magazine composition. Five styles – Roman, Italic, Bold, Mono and Stencil – form a tight, purposeful toolkit: the Mono for rhythmic editorial grids, the Stencil for identity and signage, the text styles for sustained reading.
foundry_blurb: Alcalá Xtra carries the family's defining qualities of sturdiness, legibility and economy while pushing further into small and very small sizes through a more generous x-height. Conceived as a structured set of complementary tools – Roman, Italic, Bold, Mono and Stencil – each style addresses a specific editorial demand without multiplying variants for their own sake, making the family especially at home in press contexts.

name: Pinokio
classification_notes: Geometric type system structured around a single variable – serif length. Four families move from serifless (Sans) through three progressively more slab-seriffed variants: Petit, Moyen and Grand. A fifth hybrid, Pinokio Mix, bridges the spectrum. 17 named OpenType stylistic sets (Fantasy, Eternity, Wizard, Unicorn, Amulet, Hydra, etc.). Extensive Latin coverage, 500+ languages.
summary: A geometric slab system built around a single variable – serif length – running from bare sans through Petit, Moyen and Grand, with 17 named OpenType stylistic sets and Latin coverage across 500+ languages.
description: Designed by Tanguy Vanlaeys and released by 205TF in 2025, Pinokio is structured around one idea: the progressive growth of the serif. Four families span from a clean geometric sans through Petit, Moyen and Grand, each more slab in character than the last, creating a system that covers text and display without a break in logic. Seventeen named stylistic sets – Fantasy, Eternity, Wizard, Unicorn among them – give the collection a distinct, slightly fabulist personality that sits alongside its structural rigour.
foundry_blurb: Pinokio is described by 205TF as a typographic chimera: a geometric sans-serif that progressively reveals longer slab serifs across its four core families. The Sans features vertically cut diagonals; Petit, Moyen and Grand carry increasing serif presence suited to progressively larger settings. Each family spans eight weights with matching italics, with a hybrid Mix variant bridging the full range – 80 styles in total.
